scenes.headline: Loops & Conditionals
scenes.subtitle: The control flow that gives your programs their logic
scenes.narration: Loops repeat work and conditionals make decisions, and together they give your programs real logic and control.

scenes.headline: The control tools
items: break and continue to steer loops
scenes.narration: The if, elif and else keywords let your program choose different paths depending on a test. A for loop walks through the items of a sequence one at a time. A while loop keeps running as long as some condition stays true. And break and continue give you fine control, letting you exit a loop early or skip straight to the next iteration.

scenes.headline: Filtering readings in a loop
scenes.narration: We start with a list of sensor readings. The for loop hands us each value in turn, and the inner if statement checks whether that value is above twenty. Only the readings that pass the test get printed, which is a filtering pattern you will use constantly in data work.

scenes.headline: How a for loop runs
scenes.narration: A for loop takes the next item from the sequence and runs the block of code beneath it. It then asks whether any items remain, and if so it loops back for the next one. Once the sequence is exhausted, the loop exits automatically without any manual counter.

scenes.headline: for versus while
scenes.narration: Reach for a for loop when you already know the collection you want to iterate over, since it handles the counting for you. Choose a while loop when you need to keep going until some condition changes, such as retrying a request. The trade-off is that a while loop can run forever if the condition never becomes false, so you own the exit.

scenes.text: Conditionals decide and loops repeat; master both to express any data-processing logic.
scenes.narration: Keep in mind that conditionals decide and loops repeat, and once you combine the two you can express the logic behind any data transformation.
